Stern kalute. Himmel enutaku. ... Vater papá. Mutter māma, mamá. Kind nutái. Grossvater atú. Grossmutter atší. Mutterbruder uá. Aelterer Bruder ezotapi. ... Bogen intai. Pfeil neita. Kanu itsá. Ruder etene. Steinbeil ápi. Wundkratzer piuá. ... Hängematte amaká. Tuch amakaruti. ... Kamm palatá. Weiberdreieck zapalakú. Flöte kulutu. ... Kaiman yaká Fisch kupati. Piranya yakuakumá. Mereschu kulupéi. ... Batate uhú. ... Tabak höká. Baumwolle ayupe. ... rot hemirzá. gelb (ipiulá), imi (?). weiss kisuá. schwarz ärze. ... 1 pauá. 2 mepiama. 3 kamaukula. ... 7 mepiama taputá. ... 16 papáluka nehimaka. ... 20 kumá nehimaka. Negation aitzá.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim in held page images of pp. 529-530. Kustenaú is an extinct Xinguan Arawak lect whose entire documentation is von den Steinen's 1884/1887 wordlists; Glottolog has zero descriptive references beyond the 1894 wordlist. The only later study (Corbera Mori & Ferreira 2022, downloaded now from Editora UnB open access) works from the same list, restates the 'unmarked = penult' convention (pp. 58-59) and gives no stress analysis. No description states a stress rule, so not determinable from the transcription convention plus item-by-item marked deviations is the correct and final coding; nothing better can exist. Optional housekeeping only: add the 2022 chapter to the record's 'also checked' sources.

sources.quote: 'Em relação à representação do acento no Kustenau, Steinen menciona que, nos casos em que ele não é indicado, ocorre na penúltima sílaba da palavra.' No further analysis of stress anywhere in the chapter (searched acent/sílaba/tônic/prosód); the chapter reconstructs only the segmental inventory /i e ɨ u a/, /p t k m n s ʐ h ts tʃ ɾ l w j/ and treats Kustenau as a variant closest to Waurá.
sources.locator: pp. 58-59 (stress sentence straddles the page break); phoneme inventory p. 67
